author: Pallas, 1811
status: 나그네새 수만 마리 · 여름철새 수백 마리
habitat: 숲의 나무 위, 삼나무·소나무 숲, 마을과 인가 근처의 외딴 나무

months.note: 봄과 가을에 지나가며, 번식지에서는 5~6월에 알을 낳는다.

summary: 봄과 가을에 전국을 흔히 지나가는 나그네새이다. 홀로 또는 암수가 함께 주로 나무 위에서 지내며 이동할 때에도 무리를 이루지 않고, 폭 넓은 부리로 날면서 곤충을 잡는다. 삼나무·소나무 숲이나 마을과 인가 근처의 외딴 나무에 둥지를 틀어 5~6월에 한배에 알 4~5개를 낳고, 번식이 끝나면 어린 새를 데리고 가족 무리를 이룬다. 구북구 동부, 몽골 북부, 아무르, 우수리, 만주, 사할린, 일본, 쿠릴 열도, 인도, 히말라야, 중국 서부 등지에서 번식하고 중국 남부, 하이난섬, 인도차이나, 미얀마, 인도, 말레이반도, 필리핀, 보르네오 등지에서 겨울을 난다.

art.subject: Asian Brown Flycatcher (Muscicapa dauurica), adult (sexes alike), as seen on spring and autumn migration in Korea: plain grey-brown crown, nape and back without streaks; large dark eye set in a conspicuous white eye-ring; greyish-white lores; brownish-grey ear-coverts and neck sides; wings dark grey-brown with narrow pale fringes to the tertials and greater coverts; throat whitish, breast and flanks washed pale brownish-grey, belly and undertail coverts off-white, with no streaks anywhere below; tail dark grey-brown with paler outer edges. Bill broad and flat at the base, blackish-brown on the upper mandible and at the tip, the lower mandible mostly pale grey or yellowish-brown; brown iris; short blackish-brown legs.
art.pose: perched on a branch, about to sally out after a flying insect
art.scene: Korean pine and cedar woodland with a lone tree at its edge, during spring or autumn migration; no people, buildings or text
views: adult, side view perched upright on a bare twig: plain grey-brown upperparts, white eye-ring, greyish-white lores, brownish-grey cheeks, neck sides and flanks, whitish unstreaked underparts, dark grey-brown tail with pale outer edges, blackish-brown legs

adult, head detail in side view: conspicuous white eye-ring around the large dark eye, greyish-white lores, broad flat bill with a dark upper mandible and tip and a mostly pale grey or yellowish-brown lower mandible
art.build: Small, compact flycatcher, about 13cm, slightly smaller and slimmer than a tree sparrow; large-headed with a big dark eye and a short neck. Sits upright on an exposed twig and sallies out after flying insects, often returning to the same perch. Bill shorter than the head but broad, flat and triangular when seen from above, with a faint hook at the tip. Legs short and thin, blackish-brown. At rest the long wings reach about halfway down the tail. Tail medium length, square-ended, plain grey-brown with no white or rufous.
avoid: Do not streak the breast or flanks; crisp dark streaks belong to Grey-streaked Flycatcher (Muscicapa griseisticta), and this species is plain below.
Do not paint dark smudgy breast sides forming a half-collar or an all-dark bill; those mark Dark-sided Flycatcher (Muscicapa sibirica).
Do not add bold white wing-bars, a supercilium or any rufous in the tail or rump.
Do not paint pale or pinkish legs; they are blackish-brown.
